tidbits.text: "In 1807, Parliament abolished the slave trade" is outside evidence. "Slavery ended eventually" is too vague to count.
Ending the trade wasn't ending slavery. Slavery itself lasted in the British Empire until an 1833 law ended it, 26 years after the trade was abolished.
Equiano's book sold widely in Britain, and he traveled the country speaking against the slave trade.
Anything you learned in class that isn't in the document counts, including What You Need to Know and earlier units. In 10.1, West African kingdoms traded captured people to European ships.

exemplars.text: In Document 8, Wilberforce vows to end the slave trade, and in 1807 Parliament abolished it.

In Document 8, Wilberforce vows in 1789 never to rest until the slave trade is abolished, and Equiano gives readers the view from below deck. Their campaign took eighteen years: Parliament abolished the British slave trade in 1807, but slavery itself lasted in the British Empire until 1833, which shows how hard it was to end a system that made so much money.
